definitions.explanation: What is physically contained inside something.
The real quality or meaning of something.

examples.japanese: {箱|はこ}の{中身|なかみ}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.english: What are the contents of the box?

examples.japanese: {見|み}た{目|め}より{中身|なかみ}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: Substance is more important than appearance.

examples.japanese: {袋|ふくろ}の{中身|なかみ}を{出|だ}す。
examples.english: I take out the contents of the bag.

examples.japanese: {中身|なかみ}が{空|から}っぽだ。
{中身|なかみ}を{見|み}せてください。
{彼|かれ}は{見|み}た{目|め}はいいが、{中身|なかみ}がない。
examples.english: He looks good but has no substance.

examples.japanese: {話|はなし}の{中身|なかみ}が{薄|うす}い。
examples.english: The content of the story is shallow.

examples.japanese: {形|かたち}より{中身|なかみ}を{大切|たいせつ}にしたい。
examples.english: I want to value substance over form.

examples.japanese: {外見|がいけん}ではなく、{中身|なかみ}で{人|ひと}を{判断|はんだん}するべきだ。
examples.english: You should judge people by their substance, not their appearance.

examples.japanese: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}の{中身|なかみ}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{出|だ}して、{掃除|そうじ}した。
examples.english: I took out all the contents of the refrigerator and cleaned it.

notes: Used for both physical contents and figurative substance. Compare with {内容|ないよう} which is more abstract.
